about: The world-by-year table (felix/windward-1700-preview). One row per era the game can show the real coast in. src/world-year.js turns a year into a plain description of that world (water level, which rocks are hidden, which settlements and how big, which marks, names, boats); src/world-year-build.js turns the description into a scene. Adding an era (1905, say) is a new row here plus its data file, not new code. game.js does not read this yet.

waterOffset.note: the sea stood this many real metres higher against the land than today (our arithmetic on SMHI's rate, range 0.45-0.70; docs/WORLD-1700.md section 3)

hiddenRocks.note: rocks awash today are just under the surface in 1700: still solid for a keel, no longer plainly visible

seaMarks.note: only cairns and painted rocks are drawn; the one spar mark (Hattan, invented) has no model yet and is not drawn

settlements.note: a cottage stands for about two households (poor strandsittare shared small plots); a size class with no count uses the table; the table is OUR bracket between the two nearest documented counts, not a source figure

names.note: only documented old forms are used; a place with none shows no name

boats.note: quiet coast (docs/WORLD-1700.md section 5): few boats, one or two aboard each

waterOffset.note: a few centimetres: our arithmetic on SMHI's uplift rate over 75 years (docs/WORLD-1950.md)

lights.note: only the lights standing in 1950; each carries lit / manned (keepers) from the data

islandsberg.why: the game's Islandsberg tower IS the old 1883 keeper's-house light, extinguished in 1938 (docs/WORLD-1950.md B). The new automatic concrete tower 425 m north was lit in 1950 but has no model, so the lab shows the old house dark

maseskar.why: the dwelling was painted red in 1865 (S16); its 1950 colour is not documented: red is the designer's choice

map.note: 1950 buoyage was by COMPASS SIDE of the fairway (red N/E, black S/W; docs/WORLD-1950.md C), not port/starboard by vessel. Today's OSM marks carry IALA's side as seen from the sea; for the mostly west-to-east fairways of this coast port = north, starboard = south, so port -> red and starboard -> black (the data file gives the same pairing). A mark picks cone buoy or pole by a hash of its id. isolated_danger -> the red-and-black banded 'kryssprick'. cardinal, special and the 41 minor lights are not drawn (no model / not in 1950).

seaMarks.note: the OSM marks are today's IALA A marks; the period look and which kinds existed come from the 1950 data

settlements.note: one game house stands for about 25 people (stylised; a real village has far more houses than fit); capped at 28; a size class with no count uses the table. The table and the 25 are OUR scale, not source figures. Wall colours (white, 'English red', ochre) follow the municipal preservation advice quoted in docs/WORLD-1950.md E, which is NOT a 1950 survey: uncertain.

industry.note: fish-canning factories with a dated operation in or spanning 1950: Gullholmen (Hallgren, from 1864; its 1950 status is conflicting in the sources: uncertain) and Hälleviksstrand (Bovik, 1934-1976). The other three entries are undated photos or titles and are not drawn.

boats.note: busier than 1700 (wooden fishing fleet, first leisure boats) but nothing like today; counts are our recommendation (invented), see docs/WORLD-1950.md

settlements.note: the game's own village placement (src/coast-world.js placeCoastVillages), unchanged
